list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this bounty opened (the two agree on every name, description and grade). 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation until earned.
online_note: This trophy list has no online trophies. The filter still lists Online so you can see that for yourself: it will always show 0.
sources_note: Every guide below is written in our own words from the official trophy description. Where a guide mentions a count (for example 250 stunts, 42 Shooting Range challenges), that count comes from the official description or from the PSN count PSNProfiles lists for that trophy. Anything beyond the description is labelled 'our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game' — the game is new and no location or step here is presented as confirmed in-game.

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for this one. Work through the roadmap in order: story first, then side strands, collectibles and activities, and the money trophies last, ticking each off here as you go. If your count stalls, use the filters to see which kind is left — most players finish with a collectible or activity count. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first mission of the game, so this is the first trophy most players earn and it cannot be missed in practice — just play the story from the start. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: do not skip the opening mission's prompts; the trophy pops when the mission completes. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies unlock on the chapter's final mission, so keep playing the story in order and this pops at the end of the chapter. Treat it as story-gated: it names one chapter, so earn it while you are in Chapter 1 rather than leaving the story for later. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it unlocks when the chapter's last mission ends, so play the story straight through. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: if you are doing side activities, do them between chapters rather than in the middle of a chapter's mission chain, so the chapter trophy is never far behind you. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. The name says it: this is the chapter where the story reaches Vice City proper, and the trophy pops on its final mission. Keep the story moving and it comes on its own; use this checklist to confirm you have the earlier chapter trophies first. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so by the time it pops you are one mission away from the gold story trophy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: before starting the final mission, check the missables page here — the side-strand finals are best finished before the story ends. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the game's final mission. This is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the story — after it, only free-roam cleanup remains. Before you start it, finish the side strands and any story-gated trophies you still need, because the description gives no second chance at the finale itself. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run. The description names exactly one mission, so there is no grinding involved — reach it in the story and finish it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: mission trophies like this one pop at the mission-complete screen, so if it does not pop, the mission was not yet finished. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are usually the big set-pieces of a chapter, so expect this one to take longer than a standard mission and to unlock only after its setup missions are done. Play the story in order and it will come to you; do not look for a heist to start in free roam. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play. The description names the mission and nothing else, so the guide is simple: reach Child's Play in the story and finish it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: if a mission trophy has not popped, check this list to see whether you are on the right mission — several mission names sound similar. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners. One mission, one trophy — finish Headliners and it unlocks. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: keep a save from before a big mission when you can, so a failed run costs you minutes, not a chapter. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the game's airport, so expect this mission to take place there — but that is our own reading of the name, not yet checked in the game, and the trophy itself only asks you to finish the mission. Reach it in the story, complete it, and the trophy follows. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a larger coordinated mission; whatever its shape, the trophy asks only that you finish it. It is the last of the named-mission trophies in this list, so once it pops your remaining story work is the chapters and the finale. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own completion tracker — the second gold trophy, and the real endgame. In GTA games 100% means the story plus a set list of side tasks (missions, activities, collectibles); the in-game stats screen shows your percentage, so check it there rather than guessing. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: leave this until every other trophy is done, then use the in-game checklist to find the last few percent — it is almost always a collectible or activity count. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida. The count is the whole guide: 250 is a large number, so do not grind it in one sitting — stunts happen naturally while driving, jumping and riding, and the game counts each one. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: ramps, jumps and near-misses while travelling between missions add up fastest, and a stunt-heavy vehicle helps; check your count in the in-game stats. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 250 stunts).
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game at least once. PSNProfiles lists 9 activity types, so the job is a sampler, not a grind: one fishing trip, one race, one bowling game, and so on through the nine. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: use the other activity trophies as your checklist — each one you chase for its own trophy also counts as one activity type tried here. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 9 activity types).
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PSNProfiles lists 42 of them. This is a skill trophy, not a count trophy: each challenge must be cleared at gold standard, so expect to replay the harder ones. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: learn one weapon's challenge at a time, use the range's own scoring feedback, and leave this until you are comfortable with the shooting controls. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 42 Shooting Range challenges).
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations — PSNProfiles lists 14 locations. You must win, not just finish, at every one, so this is 14 separate wins. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: learn the course on a practice run first, then race to win; tick locations off here as you win them so you can see which of the 14 are left. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 14 locations).
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word 'different' matters: winning the same race 20 times does not count — you need 20 distinct races won. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: work through the race list methodically and tick each win off here, since the game may not show a single 'races won' counter for distinct races. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a head-to-head fishing contest, not free fishing — find the challenge, then out-fish him. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: fishing challenges usually reward patience and the right spot, so watch what Cal does first and copy the approach that scores. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game, start to end. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find and play it through. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: arcades are found around Leonida's entertainment spots — try the ones in Vice City first. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Andy is one of the side characters with a strand of missions; the trophy pops on the last one. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: side strands usually unlock as the story progresses, so if Andy has no mission for you yet, play more story and come back. Treat it as story-gated — finish it before the finale. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Like Andy's strand, this is a side character's story arc — play through Kenton's missions in order until the last one completes. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: stranger and side missions often appear as icons on the map; check the map after each story chapter for new ones. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Billy's arc ends the same way the other side strands do — with a final mission that pops this trophy. Do the strand as soon as it opens rather than saving all side content for after the story, so nothing is left stranded at the finale. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers are the game's side-quest givers, and a 'strand' is a full chain of their missions, not a single job — eight complete chains earns the silver. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: the five named side characters (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of the eight, so their strands plus three more stranger chains complete it. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 8 strands).
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Randy's strand is one of the eight stranger strands that count toward the silver, so finishing it serves two trophies at once. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: keep a note of which strands you have finished here — the checklist is the only place this guide tracks them. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand, ending with his final mission. Tyrone is the last of the five named side characters; finishing his strand closes the set of named-strand trophies. After this, the remaining stranger work is the three unnamed strands needed for the eight-strand silver. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — PSNProfiles lists 18 spots. Meditation spots are quiet places in the world; you must visit and use all 18, so this is an exploration trophy with a fixed count. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: combine this with exploring all 52 areas, since both reward travelling the whole map, and tick spots off here as you find them. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 18 spots).
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. The animal is 'unique' — a single special animal, not a species to hunt repeatedly — and Bret is the character who asks for it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: unique-animal hunts usually give a clue or a region to search, so follow Bret's strand for the lead rather than hunting blindly. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are scattered across Leonida, and a 'set' is a complete group — three finished sets earns the silver. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: collect cards as you travel rather than in one sweep at the end, and keep sets together in your notes so you know which set is one card short. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 3 sets).
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the game's in-world action tied to locations — 100 of them, so this is the longest location grind in the list. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: do it while travelling for other trophies, a few locations at a time, and let the count build up across the whole playthrough instead of grinding 100 in a row. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 100 locations).
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives scattered through activities and the world; 50 of them is a steady-accumulation trophy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: you will clear many of the 50 while chasing the other trophies, so check your count late in the game and mop up the cheapest remaining challenges then. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 50 challenges).
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Reach a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the police and escape. The partner matters — do it together, not solo. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: build the wanted level away from story missions, then break line of sight and hide until the stars clear; open countryside makes the escape easier than the city. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time. The chain is the challenge: three robberies back-to-back, and losing the wanted level between them breaks it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: plan a route past three close-together shops, rob quickly, and keep moving — do not stop to fight the police. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. 'Discover' means finding new vehicles in the world — driving or encountering 100 distinct ones. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: variety is the shortcut, so drive something new whenever you see it instead of sticking to one favourite car; vehicle shows and busy streets are good hunting grounds. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 100 vehicles).
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Defeat 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode, and all five takedowns must happen inside one activation — so pick a fight with at least five enemies close together. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: find a group of enemies in the open, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly before it ends. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. The wording is a joke about leaving by plane without a ticket — take an aircraft from the airport and leave. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this is a free-roam trophy, so try it outside missions when the airport is quiet, and expect the police to notice. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and Rhinos are the game's tanks. The trophy is about the Rhino tank: get into one and use it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this is deliberately vague, so treat it as an exploration trophy — find a Rhino, get in, and see what the game asks of you from there. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get away without ever being detected. Stealth is the whole trophy: no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, no detection at any point. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: plan the approach, go in quiet, and leave the same way — if you are spotted, leave and try again rather than fighting it out. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Five vaults, five escapes — the silver reflects the repetition and the risk. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: treat each vault as its own job with its own escape route planned before you go in, and tick them off here so you know how many of the five are done. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 5 vaults).
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, so find one on the road, stop it, take the money and get away. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: pick a quiet stretch of road for the ambush, and have your escape vehicle ready before you start. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida — PSNProfiles lists 52 areas. The map fills in as you travel, so this is a coverage trophy: visit all 52 areas, including the small and out-of-the-way ones. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: drive the coastline and the back roads, not just the highways, and combine this with the 18 meditation spots and 100 WAiNK It locations. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 52 areas).
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — PSNProfiles lists 9 gangs. One operation per gang, nine in total, so you must find every gang's operation, not just rob nine operations from the same gang. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: keep a list of which gangs you have hit here in your notes; the last gang is usually the one whose territory you have visited least. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 9 gangs).
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a small moment trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find a place to enjoy a cocktail, and take in the view. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: beach bars are the obvious spot — look for a bar on or beside the beachfront and use it. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom — in classic GTA style, straight through the glass. Go into a vehicle showroom in a vehicle and drive out through the front. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: pick your moment, line up the exit, and do not stop once you are moving; the police will follow, so have an escape in mind. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. 'Follow-through' is a bowling term — play a game of bowling at that specific alley. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: the alley is named, so find Kolt & Associates on the map rather than any bowling alley; one full game should do it. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and the game gives no count to work from. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this reads like a story or side-strand moment involving a partnership, so play the story and the stranger strands and watch for a moment where a partnership goes public. We will not invent a location for it: when the game is out longer, check the sources below for a confirmed trigger. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: The description is a riddle — 'Choices made (for better or worse)' — and PSNProfiles tracks a count of 500 for this trophy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this is likely a cumulative choices counter across the game, so keep playing and making choices; it is not something to grind in one place. We will not invent what the choices are — the count is the only concrete fact the sources give. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 500).
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: The description is a saying, not an instruction: 'Second time's the charm.' Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this most likely pops when something succeeds on a second attempt — a retry that works — so do not force it; if a mission or challenge fails once, the next success may be the one. We will not invent a confirmed trigger. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: The description is a reaction, not an instruction: 'What the hell just happened?' Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: this reads like a trophy for witnessing something strange or unexpected in the world — an easter egg or a random event — so keep exploring and it may find you rather than the other way round. We will not invent a location for it. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The two parts must combine: be in a vehicle, moving, and land a melee hit that bowls the target over. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: go slowly past a target on foot in an open area and time the swing; speed makes the hit harder, not easier. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills are money that cannot be spent directly — your contacts clean it, and $250,000 laundered in total earns this. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: marked bills come from robberies and heists, so this builds up naturally alongside the robbery trophies; launder regularly rather than letting it pile up. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: $250,000).
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. It is cumulative across every shop in the game, so normal buying counts — clothes, food, weapons, anything sold in a shop. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: do not grind this early; buy what you need as you play and it will climb on its own, and check the in-game stats for the running total. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: $100,000).
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — PSNProfiles lists 8 garages. Garages are properties you purchase to store vehicles, and you need all eight. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: garages cost money, so save this for the money stage of the roadmap after the laundering trophy; check the property listings to find garages you have not bought yet. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 8 garages).
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is in the game's phone: find vehicles, then register them through Scooter Bros, ten in total. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game: combine this with discovering 100 vehicles — every new vehicle you find is a candidate to register. Sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (PSN count: 10 vehicles).
trophies.name: On the Spot
